name: Asylum -- Refugee Status Determination (DGIE, Law No. 13ter/2014)

qualifying_event.description: An asylum seeker submits a written application to the nearest immigration office, or to DGIE headquarters in Kacyiru (Kigali). Rwanda's own government -- not UNHCR -- determines refugee status under Law No. 13ter/2014 relating to refugees.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Written application; identity documents where available; evidence supporting the persecution claim.

requirements.blocker_text: Well-founded fear of persecution, assessed by DGIE under Law No. 13ter/2014.

outcome.duration_length: temporary residence permit (TRP) valid 3 months while pending; refugee ID issued on recognition

sources.title: UNHCR Rwanda -- asylum procedure: DGIE (Rwandan government, not UNHCR) processes claims via written application to the nearest immigration office or DGIE Kacyiru; 3-month temporary residence permit while pending; 30-day appeal window to a refugee appeals tribunal, then the High Court; refugee ID grants work authorization; camp-based refugees receive health/education services, urban refugees may request camp transfer via MINEMA; Protection Desks at camps and Gikondo Community Centre (Kigali) for urban refugees

STRUCTURAL FINDING WORTH FLAGGING: unlike this dataset's Jordan, Mongolia, and Cote d'Ivoire builds -- where a non-signatory or under-legislated state leaves UNHCR running refugee determination directly under its own mandate -- Rwanda operates a GENUINE DOMESTIC asylum system: DGIE (a normal government immigration authority) makes first-instance decisions itself, with a real appeals structure culminating in the High Court, under codified 2014 legislation. work_rights is 'full' on recognition (refugee ID grants work authorization per the source) -- notably strong compared to several other countries in this dataset where recognized-refugee work rights are undisclosed or restricted. Rwanda has also historically hosted large refugee populations (from DRC, Burundi, and historically its own returnee population) and runs both camp-based and urban-refugee tracks with distinct support structures -- disclosed as a structural feature rather than modeled as separate routes, since both lead to the same underlying legal status.
